audit_statement: Among the 14,038,400 possible cross-dataset image pairs (3,200 RFMiD images × 4,387 internal reference images), 8,266 pairs (0.0589%) met the DINOv2 cosine-similarity threshold of >= 0.950 and were computationally evaluated with circular FOV-masked float32 SSIM, NCC, and ORB RANSAC homography. Exactly 78 pairs triggered automated sensitivity screening flags (63 SSIM >= 0.85, 4 ORB inliers >= 20, 4 pHash <= 4, 7 DINOv2 >= 0.970; exact disjoint union: 78 pairs, zero overlapping flags). No duplicate was observed during direct visual review of seven selected boundary pairs. The remaining 71 flagged pairs are pending individual manual review. The other 8,188 candidates did not trigger the configured screening flags; they were not individually visually reviewed. In the 4 pairs with ORB inliers >= 20, geometric matches concentrate around the fundus-image aperture boundary notch or low-contrast fields rather than corresponding retinal structures; available metadata do not establish a camera-specific cause. No image duplicates were confirmed in the recorded checks. Patient-level overlap remains unverifiable from the available metadata. No model retraining, new model inference, or threshold changes were performed during the final audit-correction pass. An earlier exploratory inference run evaluated the frozen checkpoints on all 3,200 RFMiD images; those external-evaluation results remain exploratory. The internal test cohort was also evaluated during earlier ten-class baseline experiments and is not a pristine confirmatory benchmark.
